Net: A on top of C, B left of C, D right of C, E right of D, F below C.

Fold: C front. A folds up (top), F folds down (bottom), B left, D right, E folds to back.

Opposites: A-F, B-D, C-E. So opposite C is E.

Check candidates: P: top A, front C, right B. With C front, A top, right should be D. So P wrong. Q: top A, front C, right D — correct! R: top A, front F, right D — F opposite A, impossible. S: top C, front E, right A — C top, E front: E opposite C, impossible. T: top B, front D, right F — B opposite D, impossible. U: top F, front C, right D — F opposite A... F top, C front, D right: check adjacency: C front, D right, F top. Is that possible? C front, A back, F bottom... F is bottom when C front. So F top impossible. So Q.

Start orientation: top A, front C, right D.

Roll RIGHT: right face becomes bottom; top becomes right. So D bottom, A right, C front stays, top becomes... left face B becomes top. After RIGHT: top B, front C, right A, bottom D, left F, back E.

Roll AWAY: front becomes top; top becomes back. Front C → top. Top B → back. Bottom D → front. Back E → bottom. Left/right stay: left F, right A.

After AWAY: top C, front D, right A, left F, right A, back B, bottom E.

Roll RIGHT: right face A becomes bottom; top C becomes right. Front D stays. Left F becomes top.

Final: top F, front D, right C.
